title: Known Issues & Workarounds — Backlog + Status Tracker (Escalation Playbook v2)
body:
Purpose
- Working tracker for Known Issues & Workarounds pages used by Support/CS during triage + escalation.
- Tracks: owner, validation status (workaround verified), customer-facing wording review (“safe-to-share”), and publish timing.
- Source of truth for week 2–3 known-issues sprint execution (ENG-2841) + docs PRs.

Notes / definitions
- “Safe-to-share” means: OK to publish (or excerpt) in public help docs without exposing sensitive implementation details, customer data, security posture, or internal-only tooling.
- “Validated workaround” means: confirmed by Support Eng or SRE with at least one of: (a) reproduced in staging/sandbox, (b) confirmed in representative ticket with request IDs + logs, or (c) confirmed via dashboard evidence + mitigation outcome.
- Private/Enterprise pages often have an internal Confluence section with restricted handling; public excerpt may be “symptoms + what to collect + next steps” only.

Publishing targets
- Internal Confluence: publish as soon as validated (does not require PM-613 signoff, but DOES require Security review if it touches auth/SSO/audit logs).
- Public help docs: require PM-613 “safe-to-share wording” approval + Docs signoff.

Status legend
- Backlog: not started
- Draft: initial content exists (often in Docs PR branch)
- In validation: workaround being tested/confirmed
- Wording review: Docs + PM-613 review for public-safe language
- Ready to publish: all checks passed, waiting on scheduled publish
- Published (internal): live in Confluence
- Published (public): live on help docs
- Blocked: dependency (engineering fix, metrics/dashboard, security review)

Tracker (most recent at bottom)
Columns: ID | Issue / page title | Product / deployment | Tags | Safe-to-share (Y/N/Partial) | Owner | Validator | Validation status | Wording review | Artifacts | Target publish (internal/public) | Published (internal/public) | Notes

Include recommended client patterns (idempotency, backoff, resume strategy). Link to new dashboard panel once live.

Include strict “don’t promise RCA timeline” language.

Public excerpt should be careful about accounting details.

KI-012 | Incident-bot escalation workflow: missing required fields / bad handoffs | Internal process | incident-bot, tooling, required-fields | N/A | Miles Thornton | Rafael Mendes | In progress | N/A | Linear ENG-2843; Linear ENG-2842; GitHub incident-bot/pr_214 | 2026-02-23 / N/A | N/A / N/A | Not a customer-facing KB page; tracked here because it directly impacts known-issues triage quality. Add links to new escalation form once merged.

Operational checklist (publish gate)
- [ ] Owner assigned + backup
- [ ] “Applies to” tags complete: Hosted/Dedicated/Private, regions, model families, runtime/version where relevant
- [ ] Workaround validated (see definition)
- [ ] Diagnostics checklist included (what to ask customer)
- [ ] Comms guidance included (what we can/can’t promise)
- [ ] Safe-to-share classification set
- [ ] If public: PM-613 approval + Docs signoff
- [ ] If Private/Security-adjacent: Security review completed

Next actions (as of 2026-03-06)
- Priya: close KI-001 with final public link + add ‘what logs to request’ snippet to template.
- Amara/Owen: finalize KI-002 public wording (PM-613 signoff) and ensure SDK guidance matches PR-519 language.
- Kira/Tomáš: complete validation for KI-003 with updated runbook references from ENG-2845.
- Wei/Miles: define threshold + language for KI-004 (when Support should request incident vs handle as escalation) to align with oncall paging hygiene.
- Marcus/Kira: publish restricted internal KI-005 and add a short public “contact Support” stub if we decide later.
